brief:
Today, 15 November, is a rest day. You trained six days straight, 9 to 14 November. Push A is tomorrow, 16 November, and tomorrow morning's review puts its numbers on the card.

Legs B on 14 November was done in full, all 20 sets with every slot under its own name, and every lift met or beat the card. RDL 185 for 9, 9, 9 (asked 9, 9, 8). Leg press 200 for 11 on all three, as asked. Leg curl 157.5 for 10 on all three; the stack had 157.5, so that is its next weight. Leg extension: the card said 150, you did 157.5 for 10 on all three. You had logged 157.5 for 10 on 30 October, partly from memory, and the card should not have dropped below it; 14 November is three live sets at 157.5, so that is the weight from now on. Calf press 300 for 12 on all three, the first time every set was at 300. Ab machine 65 for 11 on all three. Ab wheel 10, 10.

No program change today. The program changed on 12, 13 and 14 November, and nothing in the 14 November log argues against those changes. With eight training days left before the deload (16 to 21 November, then 23 and 24 November) on 25 November, the job now is to keep adding reps and weight on the same lifts, so the deload and the December assessment have clean numbers to measure against. The exercise list gets rebuilt for the prep block that starts 9 December.

What comes next on legs: Legs A on 18 November is leg press 210, leg extension 157.5 for 12, leg curl 157.5 for 11, and calf press 300 for 13 on all three. Calf press is second on Legs A so it gets done before you are tired.

Still open, in one word each if you can: which calf machines does the New York gym have (standing, seated, or neither)? If calf press gets skipped again on 18 November, that answer is what replaces it. The shrug's fourth set has gone missing two of the last three Pull B nights; if it is missing again on 20 November, the card drops to three sets. Your logs are still stamped Meso 3, week 7, while the calendar says week 3 of the restarted block; if the phase tag at the top of the app is locked, the 25 November deload will not start by itself, and "Automatic (by date)" clears the lock. No bodyweight logged since 23 August (207 lb); a morning weigh-in this week would help.

If tomorrow's review does not reach the app by the time you train, the Push A card falls back to the app's own numbers, and two of them are wrong: lateral raises would show 17.5 (use 12.5 for 15 on all three) and the chest press would open with a lighter 142.5 set (use 157.5 on all three).

One question I am leaving open: you asked on 2 and 10 November whether the set counts are supported. Six muscles (front delts, rear delts, upper back, biceps, triceps, forearms) sit inside their ranges counting direct sets, but above them if every compound lift's helper credit is counted. The 10 November decision was to judge them on direct sets, and I am keeping it through this block. The consequence is that those six get more total work than the ranges say on paper. The counting gets settled when the program is rebuilt for 9 December.

Today: rest. An easy 20 to 30 minute walk or bike is fine. Eat and sleep like a training day.

block.why: Today, 15 November, is a rest day: six sessions ran on 9 to 14 November after the rest day on 8 November. It is day 19 of the block restarted on 28 October at the New York gym, week 3 of 4. The build runs to 24 November, the deload 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December; the show is 106 days away. One night arrived since the last review: Legs B on 14 November, done in full (20 of 20 sets, every slot under its own name; 7 November was also 20 of 20 counting a stand-in on the squat slot). Every lift on it met or beat the card: RDL 185 for 9, 9, 9; leg press 200 for 11 on all three; leg curl 157.5 for 10 on all three; leg extension 157.5 for 10 on all three, a step you took yourself; calf press 300 for 12 on all three. That closes the week of 9 to 15 November: six sessions, and every muscle logged its planned weekly sets except calves (6 of 9, the Legs A skip on 11 November) and traps (about 7 of 8 really done: the shrug's fourth set was missing, and the 8.5 the count shows includes half credit from a dumbbell lateral raise logged under the machine name on 9 November). A build block should look like this. No program change today. The program changed on 12, 13 and 14 November (versions 10 to 12); nothing in the 14 November log argues against any of them, and with eight training days left before the deload (16 to 21 and 23 to 24 November), more structure changes would cost the like-for-like numbers the deload and assessment are measured against. Two things are on watch with a date: the shrug's fourth set (20 November) and the calf press on Legs A (18 November). At the 25 November boundary the plan is a real deload: the app cuts the sets, and the review holds the weights at or a little under the last working weight, with no rep chasing. The 9 December prep block is where the exercise list gets rebuilt, starting with Legs B getting lifts of its own instead of sharing five with Legs A. Sessions stay 19, 19, 20, 20, 21, 20 sets. Training resumes with Push A on 16 November; the next rest day is 22 November.

If it is skipped again there, the slot becomes the calf machine this gym has, once a note says which one exists.

findings.finding: Brief and block said 14 November was the first Legs B of the block done in full; 7 November also logged 20 of 20 counting the stand-in on the squat slot.
findings.why: Both now say 14 November was 20 of 20 with every slot under its own name, and that 7 November was also 20 of 20 with a stand-in.

findings.finding: 'Seven training days left before the deload' is wrong; 16 to 21 and 23 to 24 November are eight.
findings.why: Brief and block now say eight, with the dates.

findings.finding: Traps: the verdict says the week logged 8.5 (plan met) while the block says traps fell short; the 8.5 includes 1.5 half credit from a dumbbell lateral raise logged under the machine-lateral-raise id on 9 November. Really about 7 of 8.
findings.why: Traps verdict and block now say about 7 of 8 really done, and explain the inflated 8.5.

findings.finding: The same four-week-average sentence ('low because of nights that did not happen'; 'every session on the card') was pasted into all 18 muscles; false for calves (calf press skipped on nights that happened, 30 October and 11 November) and contradicted by the shrug and calf skips.
findings.why: 'Every session on the card' removed everywhere; calves and traps now carry their own reason for the low average.

findings.finding: Leg extension: 'went to 157.5 straight away' and '157.5 is now proven' hid that 157.5 for 10 was already logged on 30 October in the smith-squat slot, and that the 13 and 14 November cards prescribed below it.
findings.why: Lift verdict and brief now say 157.5 was logged on 30 October (partly from memory) and the cards should not have gone below it.

findings.finding: Smith incline and low-to-high crossover progress claims were measured against 28 October, a 10-minute entry typed seconds apart (recalled, not measured).
findings.why: Both verdicts now rest on the live 9 November sets only and say why 28 October does not count; next-session numbers unchanged.

findings.finding: Muscles are counted two ways: six muscles over their ceilings on paper are judged on direct sets, while chest, hamstrings and calves are judged on the paper count, and the side-delt floor was cut on direct sets; the 10 November decision covers ceilings only. He asked on 2 and 10 November whether the set counts are supported.
findings.why: The 10 November decision (judge the over-ceiling muscles on direct sets) is kept through this block; changing how volume is counted eight training days before a deload would move six muscles' targets at once with no new evidence. The counting gets one rule at the 9 December rebuild.
findings.consequence: Front delts, rear delts, upper back, biceps, triceps and forearms keep getting more total weekly work than their ranges allow on paper (they logged above their ceilings in the week of 9 November) until the 9 December rebuild; this is stated in the brief.

findings.finding: If the 16 November review does not land, the engine's own Push A card disagrees with today's verdicts: lateral raise 17.5 for 12 (cross-seeded) instead of 12.5 for 15, chest press opening at 142.5 instead of one weight, dips 11 instead of 12; nothing warned him.
findings.why: Today is a rest day and the job gives a rest day no overrides; tomorrow's review writes Push A. The brief now tells him which two fallback numbers to ignore and what to use instead.
findings.consequence: If tomorrow's run fails, the card shows lateral raises at 17.5 and a 142.5 chest press opener; the brief tells him to use 12.5 for 15 and 157.5 on all three instead. Dips at 11 instead of 12 is one rep and harmless.
